solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ornament a lunatic knocked over — histrionic incident

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the word for lunatic is read backwards

parts.note: a lunatic is mad
a histrionic incident is a scene, a dramatic public outburst

explanation.surface: A madman tips over an ornament and then makes a dramatic fuss about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns MAD into DAM; add A and SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To damascene is to decorate metal with inlaid wavy patterns, a verb sense of ornamenting.

clue.text: Skilful soldiers climbing up inside passage

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within the other piece

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: OR is short for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Nimble troops scramble up through a narrow tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing up' means reading upwards; an adit is a mining term for a level entrance tunnel, which 'inside' wraps around the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit is a synonym for skilful, deft with hands or mind.

clue.text: Wreath borne by politician, a democrat

indicators.note: borne by says the letters are carried within the following words

explanation.surface: A garland is worn by a politician who happens to be a Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a poetic word for a garland or chaplet worn on the head.

clue.text: Article penned by eccentric person is a hoax

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a card is an amusing or eccentric person
AN is the indefinite article before a vowel

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written by an oddball turns out to be a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded rumour or false story, a type of hoax.

clue.text: Recount — was candidate upset, wanting speed?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to run for office is to be a candidate, so was candidate gives ran
rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a losing candidate was too slow in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RAN into NAR; 'wanting' just joins on RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate a story is to recount or tell it in sequence.

clue.text: Employees will settle under quiet old American leader — that's very plain!

indicators.note: in a down clue settling under puts this piece below the earlier ones

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower
staff are the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: Workers are content to serve beneath a former US president.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'plain as a pikestaff', meaning perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff' means utterly obvious, so the word evokes plainness.

clue.text: Loyal Irishman in charge restricting disorder

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the other piece goes inside these letters

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman
a riot is public disorder

explanation.surface: An Irish official keeps a lid on unrest out of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotic describes someone devoted and faithful to their country.

clue.text: Information on space module held by ten fellows

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions

explanation.surface: Details about a spacecraft section are being kept by ten people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places GEN above the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentlemen and fellows are both general words for men.

clue.text: Wise man encapsulating Irish image, not what it seems

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so another piece goes inside

parts.note: a mage is a wise man or magician

explanation.surface: A sage holds an Irish vision that proves deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, a deceptive image that is not real.

clue.text: Sin-adorer upsetting bishops?

indicators.note: upsetting the letters knocks them into a new order

explanation.surface: A lover of sin unsettles the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: bishops are among those who ordain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops ordain priests, so they are those who confer holy orders.

clue.text: Bad feeling bird gets by river

parts.note: an egret is a heron-like wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird beside a river is made miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Regret is a feeling of sorrow or remorse, a bad feeling.

clue.text: Paper transported as liquid? Fantastic notion!

parts.note: liquids are piped through pipes
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Paper turned into liquid would be a crazy idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is an unrealistic hope or fanciful idea.

clue.text: One of eight getting a bit of luck?

definitions.meaning: in rowing the oarsman setting the pace in an eight-oared boat
as in a ... of luck, a fortunate occurrence

explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew; 'getting' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke names the pace-setting rower and also completes the phrase about good fortune.

clue.text: Football team lead by little devil? They are getting better

indicators.note: lead by puts the second-named piece in front, at the top of this down answer

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
Rovers is a common British football club name, such as Blackburn Rovers

explanation.surface: A football side is captained by a mischievous character.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvers are those who are making progress or making things better.

clue.text: Like many an old family home in Lancaster needing repair

definitions.text: Like many an old family home

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many old family houses in Lancaster, a northern English city, are run down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral means inherited from forebears, as a family seat is.

clue.text: Army branch with purpose-built vehicles practises

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a branch of the British Army
hearses are vehicles made specially for carrying coffins

explanation.surface: A corps of soldiers drills using specially made vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance before giving it.

clue.text: Cave in garden, front invisible

indicators.note: with the front of the word unseen, only its tail end is used

explanation.surface: There is a grotto in a garden, its entrance hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; drop the front of 'garden' to leave its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a cave or hollow used as a lair by an animal.

clue.text: Fingerprint expert

definitions.meaning: as in a ... hand, someone skilled

explanation.definitionFit: Dab is slang for a fingerprint and also means a skilled person.

clue.text: Fellow that's set up number 500 may get gesture of approval

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A man who was framed gets the go-ahead after a large count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow that's set up' is a second route: DON (a fellow, a university teacher) set up in this down clue reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod is a bow of the head signalling agreement or approval.

clue.text: Chap taking lead at sea? Could be Nelson

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor takes command at sea, perhaps like Admiral Nelson.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson suggests the admiral, but it is Nelson Mandela, the South African leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela is an example of someone with the first name Nelson.

clue.text: Out-of-form team in no position to score goal

definitions.text: in no position to score goal

parts.note: a player who is off is out of form
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A struggling team cannot get into place to score.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an offside player is positioned illegally so a goal cannot count.

clue.text: Matrimonial duties? Adam falls short

indicators.note: falls short means the word is cut and loses its last letter

parts.note: Adam Bede is the title character of George Eliot's novel

explanation.surface: Adam fails in his marital obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam' points to George Eliot's novel Adam Bede; the definition is playful, as in the marriage bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed stands for married sexual relations, as in sharing a marriage bed.

clue.text: Rising Greek character, celebrity to come out

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a name is a famous person

explanation.surface: A rising Greek star is about to reveal themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the whole run ETANAME into EMANATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Plunged into wine, fish swam!

indicators.note: plunged into means put inside another piece

parts.note: red is red wine
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish dropped into wine went swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swam' is not the fish swimming but a head reeling, spinning dizzily.
explanation.definitionFit: When the head swims it reels, staggering or whirling with dizziness.

clue.text: Chinese fare not distinct — a problem?

parts.note: dim means faint, not distinct
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone asks if vague Chinese food is an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum is a Chinese meal of small steamed or fried dumplings.

clue.text: TV technique means eccentric noise may be heard

indicators.note: may be heard says the words are said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: fey means eccentric and a din is a noise

explanation.surface: A TV method means a strange sound might be picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: FEY DIN said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fade-in is a film and television transition where the picture gradually appears.

clue.text: Laugh at what's conveyed by madder ideas

indicators.note: what's conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters carried inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Laughing at what crazier notions communicate.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in "what's", but that word belongs to the indicator: "Laugh at" alone is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, laughing scornfully.

clue.text: Woman, one old-fashioned, is backed up

parts.note: Val is a woman's name
I is the Roman numeral one
dated means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A woman, somewhat behind the times, is given support.
explanation.definitionFit: Validated means confirmed or supported, as a claim backed up by evidence.

clue.text: Adherent to disagree about holy books

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to vary is to differ or disagree
OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A follower is inclined to argue about scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A votary is a devoted follower or adherent of a religion or cause.

clue.text: Communicators amiss, made to look silly

indicators.note: made to look silly suggests the letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Journalists, gone wrong, are made fools of.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass media are the means of communication reaching large audiences.

clue.text: Farm worker needing exercises with restrictive back

indicators.note: restrictive means confining, so this piece holds another inside it

parts.note: rear means back
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A farmhand with a stiff back needs some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper is someone who cuts and gathers a harvest.

clue.text: Agitated blokes in terrible fret end losing heart

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece
terrible suggests the letters are badly mixed up

parts.note: blokes are men

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Men are worked up by fretting about a bad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' looks like the anagram signal but is the definition; 'terrible' scrambles only 'fret', 'in' places the blokes within it, and 'losing heart' drops the middle of 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented means stirred up into agitation, as in fermenting unrest.
